The local branch is left \"diverged\" (your commit on the old base vs the remote's cherry-picked twin) — that's fine; the owner's next rebase skips the now-duplicate commit automatically. Single-path adds do NOT protect you when the sibling edits the same file. Consequence: your feature may already be in HEAD before you commit — check `git show HEAD:<file> | grep <your-symbol>` before assuming you still need to commit it. The local branch is left \"diverged\" (your commit on the old base vs the remote's cherry-picked twin) — that's fine; the owner's next rebase skips the now-duplicate commit automatically. Use this whenever the shared tree holds another agent's conflicting uncommitted work.\n- **Your uncommitted hunks in a shared source file can be swept into a SIBLING's commit** (the reverse direction; confirmed 2026-07-22, bead bf-3iosi). I had unstaged autoflush wiring in `src/cli/mod.rs`; a sibling doing bf-1xtr ran `git add src/cli/mod.rs && git commit` (their own single-path form!) which staged the FULL working file — my hunks + theirs — and committed my work under *their* message (`refactor(bf-1xtr): route stats & velocity…`).
